I farm small land, so I will keep the plan simple and steady. On my 3.5 mu, I will put 2.5 mu into my usual wheat-maize rotation because that fits my land, my labor, and my well irrigation, and it gives me grain in both seasons. I will keep 1.0 mu in cotton because I already know how to manage it, but I will not expand it since cotton needs more spraying and more care. I will use better seed on all three crops because on such a small area I care more about stable yield than saving a little on seed. I will fertilize wheat and maize a bit more heavily than cotton because grain is my main base, and I will use irrigation carefully since I have a well and do not want the crop to suffer at key stages. For wheat I will irrigate at wintering, jointing, and grain filling; for maize I will water after sowing if needed and around tasseling; for cotton I will water at seedling, flowering, and boll setting. I will use rotary tillage for wheat land, no-tillage for maize after wheat to save labor and catch the season, and plough for cotton to loosen the soil. This is the kind of plan I would actually follow because it is within my experience and it lowers the risk of making mistakes.
